name: אֲחֻזַּת
summary: The friend of Abimelech king of Gerar, who came with him and Phicol to make a covenant with Isaac at Beersheba (Gen 26:26–31). The name has the form of the noun אֲחֻזָּה “possession” in its construct or Philistine ending -at; scripture does not explain it, but it stands in the chapter where Isaac sojourns in the land promised to him and is envied for his wealth (Gen 26:3, 12–16).

evidence.note: “Abimelech went to him from Gerar, and Ahuzzath (וַאֲחֻזַּת) his friend, and Phicol the commander of his army.”
“We have plainly seen that Yahweh was with you … let us make a covenant with you.”
אֲחֻזָּה, the noun the name is formed as: “for an everlasting possession”.

note: Takes a.cl.af (2 tokens: Gen 26:26, the name, and Ezk 45:6, the noun וַאֲחֻזַּת “and the possession of”, which the corpus files under both keys). The -at ending may be a Philistine name form (compare גָּלְיַת); not followed up.
